title: Friday Frontiers Webinar on a National Conversation on Artificial Intelligence in Ireland
content:
We’re delighted to announce details of the first webinar of the Autumn/Winter 2026 series of Friday Frontiers. We are pleased to welcome Dr. Emma Clarke and Paula Kelly to present on two case studies from the #DiscussAI project. 

The Friday Frontiers webinars allow researchers, practitioners and stakeholders from across the broad DARIAH community, and now beyond, to learn about current research, best practice and social impact, and different tools and methods in digital humanities scholarly practice.

The webinar sessions are all free to attend, but registration is required.  Presentations are all recorded and published at a later date on DARIAH-Campus. 

The details of the upcoming talk, along with the registration details is below:

Title: Case Studies from #DiscussAI: A National Conversation on Artificial Intelligence in Ireland
Speakers: Dr Emma Clarke (Dublin City University) & Paula Kelly (Technical University of Dublin)
Registration Link: https://dariah.zoom.us/meeting/register/uSQOL_dAQWCujoTv3jqy7A

title: Transformations. A DARIAH Journal launches second issue on “The Past”
content:
How do digital methods shape the ways we understand, preserve and interpret the past? The second issue of Transformations. A DARIAH Journal, dedicated to “The Past”, brings together five articles exploring this question. Following the inaugural issue on workflows, the new issue examines both the possibilities and the challenges of working with historical sources and cultural heritage in a digital world.

As guest editors Agiatis Bernardou and Georgios Artopoulos explain in their introduction, “these contributions suggest that the past is never simply waiting to be retrieved. It must be identified, organised, connected, preserved and interpreted.”

The published articles address topical issues: information extraction from bibliographic data, data migration as a memory preservation process, data feminism in the work with historical newspapers, critical perspectives on historical statistics, the interaction between wikibase and memory institutions collections. Together, they provide novel methodological insights in the spirit of Open Science, making their datasets available for reuse.

title: Agiatis Benardou Delivers Keynote and Receives IEEE Award
content:
Agiatis Benardou, President of the Board of Directors of DARIAH, delivered a keynote address at the 2nd IEEE International Conference on Cyber Humanities (IEEE CH 2026), held in Venice, Italy, from 7 to 9 September 2026. The conference brought together researchers, practitioners and representatives of Research Infrastructures working across the intersection of digital technologies, the Social Sciences and Humanities, and cultural heritage.

On 8 September, Benardou delivered her keynote, “From User Needs to Knowledge Ecosystems: Designing Human-Centred Infrastructures for Digital Cultural Heritage”. Drawing on her experience across European digital cultural heritage initiatives and Research Infrastructures, she explored how the field is moving from individual digital tools and platforms towards interconnected knowledge ecosystems. Her central argument was that the challenge is no longer simply to build technically sophisticated systems, but to create infrastructures that become meaningfully embedded in the ways researchers and cultural heritage professionals work, collaborate and produce knowledge.

title: Job Opportunity: DARIAH ERIC seeks a Digital Learning Designer
content:
DARIAH ERIC is seeking a (Digital) Learning Designer to enhance its expertise in training, digital pedagogy and capacity building.

We are seeking individuals with a proven track record in training, both developing training materials and delivering workshops/courses for peers, in person and online, within research-focussed environments.

The successful candidate will support the further development of DARIAH-Campus, DARIAH’s online platform for open educational resources, and advise the DARIAH team on best practices in the design, delivery and evaluation of both online and face-to-face training activities. The position holder will also develop and implement protocols and practices for the evaluation of training materials.

The position holder will support DARIAH’s training contributions in current and future European projects in which DARIAH is involved (for example but not limited to ATRIUM, OSCARS, ECHOLOT, HABILITER). They will work in collaborative, international project environments, playing a central role in designing high-quality learning experiences that support user engagement, skills development, and network collaboration across a wide European partnership.

title: From Curation to Integration: What SSHOMP Can Do for Your National Research Infrastructure
content:
The SSH Open Marketplace (SSHOMP) is a discovery portal for Social Sciences and Humanities (SSH) research communities, pooling tools, services, training materials, datasets, publications, and workflows into a single searchable environment. 

But SSHOMP is not just a place to find resources: it is infrastructure you can build on. For national research initiatives, consortia, and projects, it opens up two complementary pathways that can dramatically reduce the effort required to achieve European-scale visibility — or to launch a full catalogue of digital humanities resources without building one from scratch.

The most direct way to engage with SSHOMP is to contribute your own resources. Once your tools, datasets, or services are described in the Marketplace, they become discoverable by researchers across Europe and beyond — not as isolated entries, but as nodes in a rich, interconnected network.

title: Research Data Management Tools and Strategies for Language Diversity
content:
A two-day international workshop funded by DARIAH-EU (Digital Research Infrastructure for the Arts and Humanities) bringing together UK and European-based scholars to explore how linguistically diverse and cross-lingual data can be better supported, shared and reused in the digital humanities.

Dates: 3 and 4 September 2026

Venue: Room 3.52, Edinburgh Futures Institute

Organisers: DARIAH-EU, Spanish Researchers in the United Kingdom (SRUK/CERU) and the School of Literatures, Languages and Cultures

We are delighted to invite you to international workshop on Research Data Management Tools and Strategies for Language Diversity funded by DARIAH-EU.

This workshop will bring together researchers, research managers, librarians, archivists and data management officers working in the UK and across several DARIAH member countries in Europe (France, Spain, Portugal, Austria, Germany, Ireland). The aim is to think collectively about how linguistically diverse and cross-lingual data can be better supported, shared and reused in the digital humanities, while also addressing questions of knowledge equity, linguistic inclusiveness and minority representation.

title: The scientists behind the data: investing in Europe’s data stewardship workforce
content:
EMBL brings together international partners to professionalise research data management across domains and sectors

By Isabela Paredes Cisneros and Lisa Vollmar 

Research data is only as valuable as the expertise and culture that support it. Yet across Europe, the professionals most responsible for enabling high-quality, reusable research data – data stewards – often work without standardised career paths, consistent training, or formal recognition. A new Horizon Europe project is designed to change that.

STARDAST – STewardship And Recognition for DAta Science Talent – is a four-year, €8 million Coordination and Support Action coordinated by the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) and set to begin in September 2026. 

Bringing together 19 partner institutions across nine countries, including research infrastructures, universities, and companies, STARDAST combines expertise from life sciences, particle physics, linguistics, translational medicine, biodiversity, digital humanities, and industry R&D within a single, coordinated framework.

title: Spotlight on WG DHwiki: Collaborative approaches to sustainable, community‑driven Open Knowledge Infrastructures
content:
DARIAH is delighted to publish the latest Spotlight article WG DHwiki: Collaborative approaches to sustainable, community‑driven Open Knowledge Infrastructures. This article is part of the DARIAH Spotlight campaign, a monthly series that focuses on digital scholarship within the DARIAH network.

Written by members of the DHwiki WG, this article presents the aims and first activities of this WG since its launch in November 2024.

In a short time, DHwiki has grown from a shared interest into a collaborative group with a clear purpose. What started as a process of getting to know one another’s work and experience is gradually becoming a more stable effort to support a wider community of practice. By building connections between research, GLAM, and Wikimedia communities, the Working Group aims to strengthen the role of open and collaborative LOD infrastructures in Digital Humanities.

title: New Czech–Swiss Collaboration for Digital Humanities and Language Research: the ELC-DHLR Project
content:
Czech-Swiss Cooperation of CLARIN and DARIAH Infrastructures

We are pleased to announce the launch of Enhancing Library Collections for Digital Humanities and Language Research (ELC-DHLR), a new Czech–Swiss collaborative project that brings together leading research infrastructures and libraries to improve access to and reuse of cultural and linguistic collections for research.

Funded in the framework of the Second Swiss Contribution for Bilateral relations Switzerland–Czech Republic, ELC-DHLR aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Czech and Swiss research infrastructures while advancing the integration of library collections into the European research ecosystem. The project contributes to the broader objective of reinforcing international collaboration in research infrastructures and increasing the visibility, accessibility, and interoperability of digital collections for the arts, humanities, and language sciences.

title: DARIAH-CH Training Series 2026–2027: Building Digital Skills for the Arts and Humanities
content:
September 2026 – May 2027 | Online | Fridays | 1:30-3:00PM

DARIAH-CH and its national partners are pleased to announce the DARIAH-CH Training Series 2026–2027, a new programme of online training sessions designed to introduce researchers to the methods, tools, and good practices that are shaping digital scholarship in the arts and humanities.

The series is aimed primarily at early-career researchers, doctoral candidates, master’s students, and anyone new to Digital Humanities who wishes to develop practical digital research skills. No prior technical knowledge is required.

Over eleven sessions, participants will explore fundamental topics in arts and digital humanities. The programme combines conceptual foundations with practical demonstrations and hands-on examples, enabling participants to understand both the underlying principles and their application to humanities research.

Each 90-minute online session consists of:

  • 40 minutes of theoretical introduction,
  • 30 minutes of practical demonstrations or hands-on activities,
  • 20 minutes of questions and discussion.
